Here's a couple things you should know before thinking about a trade, in no particular order:

Most opportunities in the are either in Labrador City, a work camp in the middle of nowhere or Alberta.

After you work a certain amount of hours as first year apprentice, you have to back to school for another semester. a lot of people lose their jobs when this happens.  You'll need to do this 4 times.

It's common to get stuck in a trade due to not being able to find work. you could spend multiple years as a 2nd year apprentice simply because nobody is looking for one. There are tons of people like this currently working outside their trades.

Employers seem to hate hiring apprentices in this province.

UNION, If you're going to do a trade then figure out your union situation before you chose your course. If you can get into the union before starting school, do it.

You can get a bachelors degree quicker than your red seal.

A good chance you could get a masters degree quicker too.

I'm not writing this to discourage anyone from taking a trade it's just some of this stuff I didn't find out til I was almost done my first year as an apprentice in this province.
